Language content is limited to: classification (Masa dialect fairly close to Gizey; North Masa subgroup per Melis 2019a:81), the circumstances of documentation (a few vocabulary items collected secretly at night in the late 1970s and 1980s at Gaigai Koumaire and Mogom from Zoumaya descendants), one lexical item amul 'chef' (untoned) set beside Marba [amul] with tone marks from Ajello et al. 2001:14, and an etymology of the ethnonym via munjuk azemay (Tourneux 1991:75). sources.note: Nothing on phonology; second-hand statement of the documentation level and Masa (Logone) affinity. text read on archive.org (third-party upload), file not.

sources.citation: Seignobos, Christian. 2014. La chasse/peche aux batraciens: aux origines de la vie des populations du bassin du lac Tchad? (L'exemple du Diamare, Cameroun). Anthropozoologica 49(2): 305-325. doi:10.5252/az2014n2a11 [Zenodo 5213674]
sources.note: No phonology content. Zumaya appear only as a historical people (gidigidiiru frog emblem of the 'proto Zumaya (XVIe/XVIIe siecles) du Diamare', ethnocide in the 19th c. citing Seignobos 1986, 'les Zumaya Pari' of Mindif); footnote 3 states unmarked vernacular terms are Fulfulde and other-language terms are flagged (GBM etc.) - none is Zumaya.

sources.citation: Seignobos, Christian. 2009. Les ethnonymes peuls comme revelateurs d'histoire dans le bassin du lac Tchad. Journal des africanistes 79(2): 316-333. doi:10.4000/africanistes.3093
sources.note: Nothing. Ethnohistorical study of Fulbe ethnonyms; the Zumaya appear as the former rulers of the Diamare (Zoumaya Lamorde, mayo Zumaya/Boula), source of the Mundang exonym Zamay for the Fulbe; one sentence notes the Zumaya struggled to impose 'leur langue et leurs rituels'. No Zumaya forms, no phonology.

sources.note: Endangerment overview; would only confirm speaker status/documentation level, not phonology.

sources.note: Nothing; states the language is known only from about 10 words recorded by Barreteau from probably the last speaker at Ouro-Lamorde (Maroua); shift to Fulfulde.

No Zumaya forms are used in the reconstruction; the only prosodic remark (p.~47) concerns lexical tone on nouns in the other Masa languages.

This ~10-word ALCAM list is the language's entire documentation.
